ety.text: Blend of гей (gej, “gay”) + Евро́па (Jevrópa, “Europe”). Popularised after a series of colour revolutions in post-Soviet states like Georgia and Ukraine, which led to deteriorating relations between Russia and the European Union. The term was used in Russia as the European Union and its liberal beliefs, represented by tolerance towards gay people, were blamed for the colour revolutions and perceived by nationalists as a threat to Russia.
